Critic suggestion: Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Elder Maren will be waiting for you. Find her first.
Why: Earlier review (critic #11): arriving in town gave no goal; naming the elder points the player at her (the cave exit lands beside Maren).

Critic suggestion: The trees close up that way. The cave's back up the worn path, north-east of the camp.
Why: Folds in the earlier Critic #1 note: the stop line names the way to the cave.

Critic suggestion: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back up the path to the glowing arch.
Why: Folds in the earlier note: names the landmark the player can actually see.

Critic suggestion: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops. Everyone complained. Everything worked.
Why: A list becomes a Maren line with a sting, and seeds 'they argued and needed each other anyway'.

Critic suggestion: Still here, dearie? {villain} would love you to sit by my fire forever. Don't give him the satisfaction. Give me back my chair.
Why: The current 'some roads would walk themselves' turn doesn't land; this keeps the push out the door and ends on her sting.

Critic suggestion: You start with plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable, dull. The Paths are where the power is. Buy some, then put them to work at the Deck Station.
Why: The tutorial line could be anyone's; 'darling' and a three-beat pitch make it Sable's.

Critic suggestion: Back for more potions! Equip them on your Character screen before a fight! Maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
Why: 'Potions and charms, back for more!' reads as if the potions came back; same info, cleaner.

Critic suggestion: Whatever it is, it sounds like it has been on hold for a very long time.
Why: 'Not open for business' is used three times in town; this one sets up the ghosts' customer-service voice instead.

Critic suggestion: I will be here, guarding the drawer. The drawer does not know. That is the point.
Why: A bare closing line gets one deadpan Bertram turn.

Critic suggestion: Somewhere below, very faintly, someone is rehearsing the word CHAMPION. Not yet, apparently.
Why: Second 'not open for business'; this hints at Bellows before you meet him and keeps the 'not yet'.

Critic suggestion: When you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, dear, the extras boil down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here.
Why: Same rule, in Alembic's soft voice instead of a tooltip's.

Critic suggestion: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone must defeat its owner first. The mantle, frankly, is rooting for you.
Why: Gives Pip's teaser his melodrama and a punchline instead of trailing off.

Critic suggestion: A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a fist for each. Bring your best deck.
Why: 'A hand on every card' is unclear; a fist per Path sets up the Fourth Fist event.

Critic suggestion: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Some coins for you. From the crowd. The crowd is me.
Why: Puts the replay win in Bellows' loud-then-small voice; the coins stay.

Critic suggestion: THE PUZZLE WINS THIS ROUND! (normal voice) Study the board. Try again. It's not going anywhere.
Why: The only Bellows line with no Bellows in it; keeps the advice.

Critic suggestion: After that, you can rip between any two stations. Thank you for ripping with the Express. Please keep your elbows inside the sky.
Why: The first half repeated the box before it; cut the repeat and give the sign-off a joke.

Critic suggestion: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest outside town, where you first turned up?
Why: 'Where you all started out' reads oddly; this matches the station blurb.

Critic suggestion: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Nobody opens the drawer. Protocol Three.
Why: Protocol One is already 'assess the customer's gait'; Three is unused.

Critic suggestion: The flasks all bubbled when you passed, dear. Every colour. They never do that for me.
Why: Seeds the four-colours clue as a vendor noticing it without knowing why; the red flask joke lives on elsewhere.

Critic suggestion: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Haven't seen him in years. Huh.
Why: 'Never broke, they say' is hard to parse; this keeps the crack in Brick and points at Flex.

Critic suggestion: Say what you like about His Perfection, the wells are clean. Shh. Don't, actually.
Why: Swaps a generic 'lovely day for a quest' for Primm's real reform and the watched town in one bark.

Critic suggestion: The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank, shouting about hydration.
Why: Introduces Brick by his tic before you meet him; the hook gets a laugh.

Critic suggestion: YOU WANT THE CRANK? TEN REPS! NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING! IT IS GOING GREAT!
Why: Keeps the challenge but lets the zone's exhaustion leak through the hype.

Critic suggestion: SPOTTERS ONLY. I AM SPOTTERS. ...SPOTTER. I AM ONE SPOTTER.
Why: The intro card repeated his first dialogue line word for word; this is the bible's stronger Brick joke.

Critic suggestion: HA! THE PUMP IS STILL MINE! GO HOME AND HYDRATE! THAT IS AN ORDER, NOT CONCERN!
Why: The gentle giant shows through the corrupted shouting; sets up his freed self.

Critic suggestion: "Passed out mid-rep. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... the spring of... well. Towel's on your tab.
Why: Real Mountain trail-off, and the tab joke now pays off the very small towel in the box before.

Critic suggestion: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Did the old yeti say hello? ...Don't tell me. I don't care. Did he, though?
Why: Pays off Mountain's "She'll pretend she didn't miss me" and stops repeating his "nobody's been out there in months".

Critic suggestion: I don't open doors. I take a very personal interest in a wall until it gives up."
Why: Rita already says "No tools... just lats"; Ripley gets her own tic.

Critic suggestion: Pushed by hand, by Beefcakes, since forever. (The D.N.A. once asked for exact start times. We said "morning-ish".)
Why: Seeds the Beefcake-Necrocrat rivalry in one sign line.

Critic suggestion: Run it to power the grid. No actual hamsters. The hamsters get breaks.
Why: Same joke, but now it says the Beefcakes don't, which is the zone's problem.

Critic suggestion: East to west. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Gym Rat card required; Coach Benchley sells them.
Why: Cuts the repeated "the long way" and tells the player where to get the card.

Critic suggestion: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only. Authorization takes thirty seconds, by order of the Minister of Efficiency.
Why: Plants Quota before her checkpoint scene, in her own unit of measure.

Critic suggestion: You see a regime enforcer flexing at nobody. He has held the pose since breakfast, because nobody has told him he can stop.
Why: Fixes "at nobody" vs "his audience", and the joke now carries the exhaustion under the hype.

Critic suggestion: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its folks moving. Wheels, mills... and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.
Why: Same Path facts in his voice instead of a brochure sentence; punchline last.

Critic suggestion: Fifteen concern biceps. The other two were a history of the Lifting Festival; the regime burned those, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
Why: Says what the regime burned and why it matters: the festival and the old king, which Mountain then fills in.

Critic suggestion: Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. I have practised the sigh. It is devastating.
Why: Drops a second "brain-ceps" two boxes after the first and ends on a joke in his voice.

Critic suggestion: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a little less for repeat attendance. The regime calls it a "processing fee". A D.N.A. phrase, I suspect.
Why: Says plainly that repeats pay less, and adds a rivalry jab in the Professor's footnote voice.

Critic suggestion: Not quite a set, champ! But WAIT - that wasn't a failure! That was a FREE TRIAL!
Why: Chet "never a quiet sentence": the loss line becomes an infomercial pitch.

Critic suggestion: Gym's open! The weights are not. The scales stayed, though - standard measures, from the Capital. Say what you like, they never lie.
Why: A grudging nod to Primm's genuinely good reforms (standard measures), in an ambient line.

Critic suggestion: You receive an empty cup. Flavour: surprise.
Why: Calls back the stand's own sign ("Flavour: surprise.") instead of a joke that does not quite land.

Critic suggestion: The Swole Station's lights are back on. Grid's humming. I'd make a speech, but all my energy went into the lights. Take your reward.
Why: Gus is flat and tired; "HUMMING" and a pep-talk threat read like Benchley.

Critic suggestion: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep eating my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM!
Why: "END THE BULKING ORDERS" was unclear; this keeps the instruction and the coach volume.

Critic suggestion: Just measuring. Lovely broad shoulders round here. Very roomy work, when it comes. It hasn't, lately. Heh.
Why: A quiet hint that Death is stuck, funny only once you know who Hob is.

Critic suggestion: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says, looking down. 'So those are my feet. Hello, feet.'
Why: The old line repeated his mid-fight bark word for word; this gives the payoff its own joke.

Critic suggestion: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming a training-montage tune to itself.
Why: "A boxing movie" is a real-world reference that breaks the setting; same joke without it.

Critic suggestion: Every weight the regime ever took, stacked behind one locker door. Each plate still has its owner's name chalked on the back.
Why: Turns a flat line into a small human detail: these weights belong to people and are waiting to go home.

Critic suggestion: Their squats are not regular, so neither are the rounds. Listen for the knees on the stairs.
Why: Fixes the clash with "time their rounds by their squats" and gives Flex a calm punchline.

Critic suggestion: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). It has been dusted. Recently.
Why: "Empty... remains empty" said the same thing twice; the dusting shows how sure the regime is.

Critic suggestion: Wave, and he will wave back. After the pose. The pose may take a while.
Why: Gives the freed Flex sign a joke in his patient, unhurried style.

Critic suggestion: (To town. The cardio checkpoint is a snack bar now. Snacks are mandatory.)
Why: "Stairs sold separately" was unclear; the freed zone now uses the regime's word warmly.

Critic suggestion: YOU DID IT. Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch. Best day since... since the last best day. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.
Why: Drops the gamey "rest of your HP"; keeps the warmth.

Critic suggestion: Clench is learning to lift from zero. The strongest take the longest. Yesterday he spotted Gary without being asked. The gym is open to everyone now; come whenever you like.
Why: Shows Clench's first step back instead of only stating it, and pays off Gary.

Critic suggestion: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible. Underneath it, faintly, something smells of hot iron.
Why: Plants the arms-factory secret on the very first step in, without a word of exposition.

Critic suggestion: Your HP is already full. A chef refills your plate anyway. Here, being full is treated as a misunderstanding.
Why: The current joke is muddled; this one comes straight from the zone's 'nobody leaves hungry' culture.

Critic suggestion: A hidden stash! Unsampled, unsauced and all yours.
Why: The Pantry Run summary already spends the lettuce pun; this nods to the Special Sauce instead.

Critic suggestion: You fall in the gravy. A passing chef fishes you out with a ladle and checks you for seasoning. (-1 HP)
Why: Present tense like the rest of the narration, and a chef-shaped joke instead of 'Somebody'.

Critic suggestion: The golem steps aside with the slow dignity of a roast being carved. The way is open.
Why: A flat system line gets one image of the knightly meat golems.

Critic suggestion: You ladle some soup, look at it, and pour it back. You are full. The fountain takes it well.
Why: Replaces a plain statement with a small, deadpan beat.

Critic suggestion: - Guard the kingdom (with golems. Defensive golems. Please stop saying the other word.)
Why: The brief's 'chefs flinch at the word weapon' finally appears on the zone's first sign.

Critic suggestion: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom. One wants saffron, one wants a favour, one wants a fight.
Why: Tells the player the three gate conditions at a glance, in sign rhythm.

Critic suggestion: Please do not bite the buildings. The mayor's house is down to two layers, and he knows it was a visitor.
Why: 'Load-bearing' is Bertram's owned gag; this keeps the joke local to cake town.

Critic suggestion: Four ingredients, in the right order. Anything else tastes like a lesson.
Why: The current sentence does not parse; this reads cleanly and keeps the hint.

Critic suggestion: Psst. Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it: chefs cook, golems guard. Lately the golems have been... practising.
Why: Swaps two poster slogans for a nervous hint of the war programme; Basil's voice, same fact.

Critic suggestion: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. Last cook who complained got promoted to taste tester. We haven't seen him since.
Why: Basil already does 'hears everything, never tastes'; this gives Tarragon his own fear and pays off the taste-tester signs.

Critic suggestion: I'm so hungry I looked at a Refusemancer compost heap and thought 'starter'. Don't tell anyone. I'd never live it down.
Why: Uses the Gourmand vs 'garbage eaters' rivalry from someone sincerely inside the culture.

Critic suggestion: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. They stamped my decorative cake. Right on the rosette. I have not forgiven them.
Why: The current line is hard to follow; this keeps the stamp and sets up the cake with snoot.

Critic suggestion: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. I'm not complaining. I'm fetching. They look similar from a distance.
Why: The 'send it back' turn is muddled; this is cleaner overworked-intern panic.

Critic suggestion: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have a cake to look at.
Why: Her cake is decorative; the tweak lands her running gag and its later payoff.

Critic suggestion: Back for more? Splendid. A footnote, while it simmers: the Capital's school lunches were excellent once. Hot, free, balanced. Then came the paste.
Why: Repeats his bark almost word for word; this works in Primm's genuinely good reform and Crumb's paste.

Critic suggestion: The golem stands firm, like an aspic that has made up its mind.
Why: One food image for a bare system line.

Critic suggestion: En garde! Thirty years of service, and I have never once boiled over. Until now. Yes, Chef.
Why: The event line nearly repeats his intro; this gives the half-health turn its own beat.

Critic suggestion: You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons in crates marked SERVING UTENSILS (DEFENSIVE). Take what you can carry.
Why: The euphemism is the zone's joke engine; the golems own 'overthought' ladles.

Critic suggestion: Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. A clipboard on the rail reads: BATCH 3,652. TASTED BY: (blank).
Why: Shows the corruption instead of telling it: ten years of daily batches, nobody tasting.

Critic suggestion: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every note signed by the Grand Chef is in perfect copperplate, without one gravy stain. Real chefs' notes are mostly gravy stain.
Why: Turns the clunky left-handed clue into the zone's theme: appearance over substance.

Critic suggestion: - Guard the kingdom (with golems; the cannons are ovens now)
Why: The freed sign shows the zone has changed instead of repeating the old line.

Critic suggestion: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet; we just mopped. Free samples by the door. Take two. Nobody is checking.
Why: The current line is tangled; this shows the freedom in plain sign rhythm.

Critic suggestion: Tarragon! Sous-Chef! Fetcher of things! I caught up with lunch!
Why: Pays off his running gag of never catching up with lunch.

Critic suggestion: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us. (Also: whose chin is that?)
Why: Restores the 'Whose chin is that?' half of the chin gag pair the voice bible flags for restore.

Critic suggestion: You are already as rested as the dead get, and the dead get very rested.
Why: Cuts the tail that explains the joke.

Critic suggestion: Beefcake couriers: throwing a parcel through the window is not 'delivery'. Neither is throwing the courier.
Why: A weak pun replaced by the Necrocrat-Beefcake rivalry, filed as a memo.

Critic suggestion: Per my last memo: still serving 3. Per the memo before that: also 3.
Why: Keeps the 'per my last' weariness without stopping to explain the joke.

Critic suggestion: Back again, dear? Nobody else leaves. Since the transfer, not one soul has passed on. Not even me.
Why: Generic workplace gag swapped for the zone's key fact (Death froze) in Agnes's own want.

Critic suggestion: The Records Basement elevator needs Form 13-B. I don't have one. Nobody does. I applied, but the application form is a 13-B.
Why: 'It builds character' is filler; the loop of forms is the zone's own joke.

Critic suggestion: Re-certified again. For the paperwork, the Department pays you a small processing fee. It has never paid in that direction before.
Why: Makes clear the fee goes to the player, with a dry turn at the end.

Critic suggestion: Try again. The signs aren't going anywhere. Since the transfer, neither is anyone here.
Why: Same joke, now carrying why nobody here can leave.

Critic suggestion: One correct. Your token. I have noted your potential in the margin, in very small writing.
Why: 'My interest remains non-refundable' does not quite parse; this is the examiner's drone with a turn.

Critic suggestion: I took a number. Heh. Makes a change. Usually I'm the one calling them.
Why: An Old Hob line that is funny now and funnier once you know who he is.

Critic suggestion: brb, haunting. been brb since '09. it's a long b.
Why: The current bark is muddled; this is one clean Kyle joke.

Critic suggestion: Take a number. I won't be calling it. Take it anyway.
Why: 'Irrelevant' is Mortimer's word; this is Betty's never-impressed shrug.

Critic suggestion: Agnes Overdue. Front desk, and on my lunch hour, appellant. Forty thousand appeals, every one denied. They've started decorating the stamps.
Why: 'I stopped counting' contradicts her bark (appeal forty thousand and one); she keeps the receipts.

Critic suggestion: Every important document in the Hall is stamped, signed and witnessed here. The transfer of authority was, too. The notary is still finding blue-green feathers.
Why: A quiet clue to Plume, the peacock who notarized the transfer, before the player meets him.

Critic suggestion: the queue moved. like, actually moved. agnes called my number at 3am. i was afk. she called it again. nobody's ever called me twice.
Why: The current line says his number is 400 years off, which contradicts Agnes calling every number the night the zone is freed.

Critic suggestion: Back again. The ethics questions have been returned to the building. Not yet to the exam. One reform at a time.
Why: Pays off his own setup (ethics removed, 'not in the building') instead of a flat statement.

Critic suggestion: Head of the whole Department, and still on the front desk. They gave me a big office, dear. Nobody waits in a big office. They wait here.
Why: The ghost line did not follow; this says why she stays at the desk, which is her whole arc.

Critic suggestion: The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, at the Rotheart, deep in the Verdant Dump. Everything grew out from her. Me too, the day a very tidy lady with shears came calling.
Why: Plants Clipwell (who corrupted Moss) before the mill, in Moss's shy voice.

Critic suggestion: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post. The mug is mostly apple. A goat watches every bite. HP restored.
Why: Replaces a flat third beat with the zone's goat gag; works before and after freeing.

Critic suggestion: New stairs. Same climb. And the stairs grew two more steps overnight.
Why: Puts the never-stops-growing wrongness into a worker grumble; keeps the freed pair's opening.

Critic suggestion: The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. Half our garbage is their souffle, barely touched.
Why: Seeds the Gourmand rivalry from inside the zone; the old line was filler.

Critic suggestion: The belt does not slow down for anyone. It has been asked.
Why: The old idiom was garbled; this is cleaner and lands on a joke.

Critic suggestion: A pile of tyres, doors and one very stubborn wardrobe across the gap.
Why: "Ambition" is the third junk-pile ambition in the zone; a concrete object is funnier.

Critic suggestion: A trash golem towers over you, moss coating its fridge body. Something sprouts from its ears. Inside, the little light is still on.
Why: "Cool head" is the Buffet golems' owned pun; the fridge-light image is the Dump's own joke.

Critic suggestion: We are the Refusemancers: druids of waste removal and agriculture. Our animals turn the kingdom's garbage into fertilizer for its crops. The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. They eat our carrots.
Why: Same facts, shorter, plus the rivalry and why the Paths need each other, punchline last.

Critic suggestion: Back again, dearie! Turnips are a day old. A lovely vintage, if you're a turnip.
Why: Retires the generic "Shop's open" greeting; keeps the vintage turnip gag.

Critic suggestion: The boar and goat in the stables will carry you. Ask nicely or ask rudely; they ignore both the same. Good, sensible animals.
Why: "They don't speak either" reads as a contradiction right after "I speak fluent goat".

Critic suggestion: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We... sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
Why: Restores the canon catchphrase's pause ("We... sampled it").

Critic suggestion: Normal-looking plants, mostly. A little too green. Every leaf turns, very slightly, to follow you.
Why: Shows the watching instead of telling the player how it feels.

Critic suggestion: The vines are choosing who gets through. They are reading your deck very closely.
Why: "Footing" is Coach Benchley's owned pun.

Critic suggestion: Gentlemen, if you would. He is well over regulation height.
Why: Was a word-for-word repeat of her intro line; now she sends the topiaries in with her regulation-height tic.

Critic suggestion: It tastes of rain and old boots. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.
Why: "Rain and regret" repeats the mushroom result; the boot calls back the pool's own text.

Critic suggestion: A tunnel of drifting spores. A well-built deck walks straight through. A loose one starts to sprout.
Why: Same hint, with a turn at the end instead of a rules sentence.

Critic suggestion: Light pours through the splitting Rotheart.
Why: Drops the flat "You see" camera narration the review flagged.

Critic suggestion: Wildflowers follow the light outward, field by field, through the Dump.
Why: Drops "You watch"; one concrete image.

Critic suggestion: Day-old turnips, dearie, and not one of them looking at anybody. Finally, produce with manners. Heh!
Why: Retires "Shop's open" and tightens the turnip payoff.

Critic suggestion: Archdruid Compostella. I am told what happened to the barn. I cannot remember doing it. The barn, I gather, remembers me. I will help put it right.
Why: Lands her canon barn gag (she forgets, it remembers); her bark already offers to mend it.

Critic suggestion: You have earned the truth, so here is the first piece of it: I am not only a tortoise who bakes.
Why: Restores Maren's own turn into the confession; the current line says she is hiding things instead of showing it.

Critic suggestion: I wasn't sure of you before. I am sure now. Mostly.
Why: Restores her sting in the tail; 'Mostly.' is pure Maren and keeps her guarded at stage 2.

Critic suggestion: I have been hiding here ever since, with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would ask what else they had made.
Why: Gives the bare line a concrete, sincere image: the pie was where she hid the hands that blew the glass.

Critic suggestion: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. I can hold mine for a week. They cannot.
Why: The knees joke does not follow from holding breath; a tortoise who can hold hers all week does.

Critic suggestion: The roads are open. Even I use them. I passed a hare this morning. He has asked for a recount.
Why: Earlier review (Oct 28): Maren is a tortoise again, so 'the tortoises use them' reads oddly; the joke moves onto her.

Critic suggestion: Someone has thrown a boot in the spring. The water has gone politely round it.
Why: Restores the dry running gag (the water going politely round the boot) and drops the platitude.

Critic suggestion: Every Gourmand recipe still begins with the same two words: first, water. Somebody has added 'and salt' here. Twice.
Why: Drops the 'You recall' frame; the player cannot recall a recipe, the narration can state it.

Critic suggestion: A well with opinions. Fine. I'm keeping the bottle.
Why: Restores the Wanderer's version (story bible): 'Fine.' is his undercut, and 'keeping' lands the joke.

Critic suggestion: The service-tunnel network is down. The wheels that once turned the shaft lifts have spent ten years lighting the facade instead. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.
Why: The current line says nobody runs the wheels, in a district built on wheels that never stop; this squares it and shows where the power went.

Critic suggestion: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! Flour: some. Salt: enough. Time: until it smells right. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.
Why: Uses Chef Marlo's 'some' quantities so the card reads as his, with a sharper picture of the imprecision.

Critic suggestion: The second wheel has been turning since some of its runners were too small to reach the pedals. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You pocket it.
Why: Drops 'old enough to vote' (odd in a monarchy) and the doubled hook; the image does the work.

Critic suggestion: The third wheel's crew are children in school caps. 'It is a school activity,' says a banner. Nobody has rung the bell.
Why: Narration shows instead of exclaiming 'Children!'; the bell that never rings carries the horror quietly.

Critic suggestion: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. Nobody holds a permit to sing, so they sing very quietly. Nobody stops them.
Why: Replaces the vague 'a quiet tune accompanies' with one specific, sincere act of small defiance; no joke on the beat.

Critic suggestion: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one showpiece street. The rest of the kingdom went dark.
Why: 'One small town' in narration can read as the hub town; the facade is one showpiece street.

Critic suggestion: Every house in this quarter was built to show what the whole kingdom could be if everybody simply tried harder.
Why: The line spells the district name literally in a story file (token rule) and the sign need not repeat its own heading.

Critic suggestion: To the Crease. Living passengers only. The dead have asked to come down too; we are thinking about it. Be kind.
Why: The current sign contradicts itself (the dead are not allowed down, yet the living fear the dead down there); this is clear and funnier.

Critic suggestion: The tears are temporary and fully under control. (Scrawled below: the Paths tear where {villain} forced them into one shape. His hold slipped the night someone escaped the Ministry.)
Why: An official sign would never admit his hold is failing; the fact survives as a Wrinkle's scrawl under the slogan, the Capital's core joke.

Critic suggestion: Back in one piece? Good. Hesper charges by the piece.
Why: Wren's one sharp joke per scene, and a nod to Hesper's correction fee, instead of a repeated 'one piece'.

Critic suggestion: The records say he began well. His first decree put a hot lunch in front of every schoolchild. Remember that. It excuses nothing.
Why: The archivist is the natural voice for Primm's sincere early reforms; one concrete good deed makes him tragic before the castle.

Critic suggestion: I talk to him in the parlour. He was always the patient one. I'm not, it turns out. Please, if you can help.
Why: Gives Pell her own soft dry humour about herself, never at her loss, and keeps the plea.

Critic suggestion: I have measured twelve thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
Why: 'Eleven' is the prince's story clue; a gate tally should not spend it casually. Same joke, same shape.

Critic suggestion: Still one hair above regulation. I have thought about that hair all week. Do not make me regret it.
Why: Pays off his 'one hair' from the intro and shows a small human obsession instead of repeating 'still'.

Critic suggestion: Here... from the old days. We gave these out... at the end of a shift. Remember ends?
Why: Breathless Rollo rhythm, a clearer reward line, and the quest's whole point (stopping) as the punchline.

Critic suggestion: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card. The kind with nothing written in it.
Why: One more clause turns a flat simile into the slogan-and-whisper gap.

Critic suggestion: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! Lost Ministry property must be returned at once, and not spoken to!
Why: Puts the 'escaped Royal Asset' hunt into the broadcasts; 'not spoken to' is funny early and chilling after the reveal.

Critic suggestion: Great news, citizens! The public records have never been tidier! Every untidy page has been corrected!
Why: The exit-is-the-entrance joke is already the exit guard's; this spends the broadcast on tidy records curdling into erased history, which sets up Wren.

Critic suggestion: If you remember things differently, please report to the Correction Ward. Your memory will be tidied too!
Why: Second box of the records broadcast: Plume's cheer over a real threat, pointing at a place the player can visit.

Critic suggestion: You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and twelve minutes. I have had the figure framed.
Why: 'Eleven' is a story clue; Quota's precision works with any figure.

Critic suggestion: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Sorting peel from shell, all day. Messy. You'll hate it. Good.
Why: 'Peel from shell' reads as a typo; this is clear and gives Fern her grumbly last word over the tidy hare.

Critic suggestion: Back in the Gainlands... we threw commuters. Now I'd pay... to be thrown.
Why: His other lines already say 'it was cardio'; this adds the Beefcakes' people-throwing transport and an exhausted joke.

Critic suggestion: Beefcake bore, Gourmand vents, Necrocrat signs, Refusemancer drains. The junction crew lifts the scrap. Every Garbage becomes muscle.
Why: The Four-Faction Junction is the place to show the tunnels were built by all four Paths together; keeps the Garbage-to-muscle hint.

Critic suggestion: ATTENTION! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
Why: HALT is Captain Spotless's catchphrase; Crumb barks drill-sergeant orders.

Critic suggestion: 'Welcome,' says a quiet, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet. Please wipe your opinions. You are expected.'
Why: Restores the flagged 'wipe your opinions': Primm's polish in one clause, before he appears.

Critic suggestion: All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier, and a little less themselves. I consider this the improvement.'
Why: Restores the flagged 'less themselves' beat in Primm's precise clipboard voice; also drops a stray second opening quote mid-note.

Critic suggestion: When the champion is sufficiently weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: do not underestimate him. He does a lot of stretching.'
Why: Restores the story bible's own quote (precision that is accidentally funny) and drops a stray opening quote; the margin note then answers it.

Critic suggestion: Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located! Please hold your applause until she has been removed.
Why: Plume's spin gets its turn: the slogan over the arrest.

Critic suggestion: A curator with a feather duster patrols the side gallery. Anything crooked, he straightens. Anything alive, he dusts. (A battle.)
Why: Restores the flagged 'Anything alive, he dusts' and drops the 'You see' narration.

Critic suggestion: A clerk at a tall desk, stamping everything that moves. Quite fast. Quite sad. His eyes never leave the paper. (A battle.)
Why: Restores 'Quite fast. Quite sad.' (flagged) while keeping the tested 'His eyes'.

Critic suggestion: A staircase so grand it has its own staircase. Every step is exactly the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
Why: Restores the flagged image; 'You face a vast staircase' is placeholder narration.

Critic suggestion: You leave the seed where it fell. Out of its dome it looks smaller. Most things here do. You go back.
Why: Gives the wing a closing image (his works shrink once looked at) instead of a bare exit line.

Critic suggestion: You sit in the old reading chair. It is worn exactly where one person sat, every night, for years. Someone made the lampshade by hand. It is a little crooked.
Why: Puts back the flagged human detail and ends on 'crooked', the game's word for freedom, in Primm's own room.

Critic suggestion: They are good. They are so good. You roll up the best and take it, with something in your throat.
Why: Restores the flagged 'They are so good' motif: Primm began as a good man.

Critic suggestion: You prise off the old gold frame and leave the mirror hanging, bare. It still shows whoever stands in front of it. It never needed the gold.
Why: The current line reads like a receipt; this keeps the gold and lands the room's point.

Critic suggestion: A little brass plate for donations to {villain_title}, bolted to the wall. It is quite full. You take the lot.
Why: Restores the flagged dry 'It is quite full' (token kept).

Critic suggestion: It is, after all, other people's money. They would want it back.
Why: Restores the flagged wry justification; the current line just restates the action.

Critic suggestion: At the top, a pot of coins sits on the landing: a tip left by the last person who made it. You rub your legs and pocket the coins.
Why: Restores 'the last person who made it', which says what 500 identical steps cost.

Critic suggestion: It goes on. They are good. They are so good.
Why: Restores the flagged motif; 'Page after page describes work that helped people' tells instead of shows.

Critic suggestion: Once, he was exactly the person you would want running a kingdom. You close the last journal very gently.
Why: Restores the flagged line that makes Primm tragic before the Last Journal.

Critic suggestion: Sorry. That's forest mud. I've walked a long way, and everyone I met on the way here was afraid of you.
Why: Restores the flagged first words to Primm: the Wanderer's own voice answering 'you have scuffed it'.

Critic suggestion: Every one of them has a number. Nobody is ever overlooked. Do you know how few kingdoms can say that?
Why: Restores Primm's flagged sincere, faintly proud question: numbering people as his gift.

Critic suggestion: This will not hurt. It will, however, be Standard.
Why: Restores the flagged line: gracious, precise, and it names Phase 1 (Standardization).

Critic suggestion: Because some things are five. Some people are.
Why: Restores the direct answer to 'Why must anything be five?' (flagged callback).

Critic suggestion: Because some things are five. Some people are.
Why: Same callback in the rushed variant.

Critic suggestion: And nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Why: Restores Agnes's closing-line callback (story bible section 21) and keeps the tested phrase.

Critic suggestion: Nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Why: Same Agnes callback in the Necrocrat-only variant, where she was certainly heard.

Critic suggestion: Grandmaster Flex steps out from behind a pillar, unwinding a very small bandage from a very large arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
Why: Restores the flagged image and drops 'You see'.

Critic suggestion: The Grand Chef, in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? No. Of course you have not.'
Why: Restores her flagged voice: she answers her own question, as only she can.

Critic suggestion: 'It applies to him, dear. It applies to him very well.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
Why: Restores the flagged Agnes line (her technicality, with relish); rule text unchanged.

Critic suggestion: The model lies in pieces. A hundred thousand tiny houses on the floor, all in the wrong places, and somehow they look better.
Why: Restores the flagged image: mess over perfection, the game's thesis in one sentence.

Critic suggestion: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting it go anyway. Watch.
Why: Restores the flagged answer: he shows Primm the letting-go instead of describing it (the earlier 'Watch how it's done' trimmed so it cannot read as a gloat).

Critic suggestion: The mirrors crack one by one, and for the first time in ten years {villain} sees himself in them.
Why: Drops the 'You hear' frame the earlier pass added; the image speaks for itself.

Critic suggestion: No crown. No perfect smile. Only a tired man kneeling above a very small kingdom.
Why: Restores the flagged three-beat caption; the current one buries 'tired man' mid-sentence.

Critic suggestion: Light pours in through the broken glass. It does not feel like winning. It feels like the end of a long, quiet lie.
Why: Restores the flagged 'end of a long, quiet lie' (the story bible quotes it), in present tense.

Critic suggestion: The Necrocrat wing's archive is paper from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
Why: Fixes 'is filing from floor to ceiling' (reads as a typo).

Critic suggestion: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. The fee is still yours. The tea is not free just because the kingdom is.'
Why: Restores the flagged Hesper sting; the current line explains itself.

Critic suggestion: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Won't. Waste of good water. Come back any time.
Why: Same joke, half the words, in Fern's grumble.

Critic suggestion: We're well. My husband would have said you were late. He'd have meant it fondly.
Why: Restores the flagged Pell line; the current one repeats her intro ('every morning').

Critic suggestion: And chaotic. There is flour on the ceiling. I have never been so happy to have a mess.
Why: Restores the flagged line: 'everything in its proper place' is the regime's value, not liberation's.

Critic suggestion: I am going to wear a hat of any size. Maybe two at once.
Why: Restores the flagged freed joy (One Approved Hat Size pays off with two).

Critic suggestion: The bakery is painted on. There is going to be a real one, as soon as someone learns to bake. I have a recipe. The recipe is: try.
Why: Restores the flagged punchline; the current line ends flat.

Critic suggestion: The hedge is round. The hedge wanted to be round. I asked it. I did not have to submit a form.
Why: Restores the flagged payoff to the square-hedge setup; giddy and specific.

Critic suggestion: Spontaneity every day! I am exhausted! I am not sure I like it! I love it!
Why: Restores the flagged crooked joy; the current version is plain cheer.

Critic suggestion: I am not going to be polite today. I am going to be honest. Your hat is awful. I love it.
Why: Pays off her 'I am the politest person in the Showcase' setup (flagged).

Critic suggestion: Attention, citizens. (a cough) The weather is no longer approved. It is just weather. It seems to be managing.
Why: Pays off the running gag (Plume approving the weather) on the same speaker slot that set it up.

Critic suggestion: Attention, citizens! Hats of any size are now permitted. Hats of negative size remain under review.
Why: Restores the flagged freed hat gag, still in broadcast voice.

Critic suggestion: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now every day. You may stop rehearsing your surprise.
Why: Undoes the 'rehearse your surprise' setup directly (the voice bible's freed-announcement rule).

Critic suggestion: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank anyone who exists.
Why: Turns 'Please report anyone who exists' into its payoff.

Critic suggestion: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I thought I might go for a walk. If that is... No. I am not asking. I am telling you. I think.
Why: Shows the running gag (almost asking permission) instead of stating it.

Critic suggestion: The scale model cracks in half. Then the table cracks. Then, with the sound of a very large drawer being pulled from a very large cabinet, the castle walls begin to come down.
Why: Restores the precise, filing-cabinet image of Primm's castle falling; the current 'You hear' line is flat.

Critic suggestion: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat, and a very surprised citizen steps through it onto a very real street.
Why: Restores painted door versus real street (the facade theme) and drops 'You see'.

Critic suggestion: Fig Sly comes up out of the Crease already selling something, to somebody, for some reason. Nobody stops him.
Why: Narration about him, not his line: restores the story bible beat ('already selling something') over a flat description.

Critic suggestion: The Beefcakes are late. The Necrocrats have brought a form. The Gourmands are overdressed. The Refusemancers smell, faintly, of compost.
Why: Restores the four Paths arriving in character (story bible beat 7); the current line is generic.

Critic suggestion: Muscle and stoves, records and soil: each was good alone. Together they ran a kingdom, argued about it every day, and it worked.
Why: Restores the game's thesis, which sets up 'The point was the argument' in the next box.

Critic suggestion: Somebody has crossed out MAY and written SHOULD. Somebody else has crossed out SHOULD and written WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. A pigeon sits on the full stop.
Why: Shows the four hands arguing on the wall instead of summarising it; the pigeon is the quiet last turn.

Critic suggestion: In memory of Form 27-B, Form 27-C and Form 27-B
Why: Credits may carry a joke: restores the forms callback over a generic dedication.

Critic suggestion: No hats were harmed. Several were enlarged.
Why: Restores the regulation-hat callback; the credits had two near-identical dedications in a row.

Critic suggestion: I have filed a Form of Gratitude, dear. It was approved on the first attempt. Irregular.
Why: Pays off Agnes's 'Irregular.' gag and her denied appeals; the next box ('going to cry') stays sincere.

Critic suggestion: The Pathwork Throne
Why: Title case, like every other beat title; the lower-case 'the' is a slip from the earlier pass.

Critic suggestion: Maren pushes through the crowd, tortoise-slow, and stops in front of you. There is flour on her sleeve.
Why: Keeps the flour, drops 'You see', and lets her slowness show how hard she is pushing.

Critic suggestion: He designs very good drains, it turns out. Do not tell him I said so.
Why: Current line has the guard call himself 'the guard'; this one also quietly withholds the praise Primm wants.

Critic suggestion: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says thank you. That's what the 'Hm' meant. Thank you from me, too.
Why: 'Dad says a lot' contradicts the man who just said 'Hm.'; this reads his 'Hm' instead, warmly.

Critic suggestion: In the Capital's square, the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Nobody trips. Several people cry.
Why: Drops 'you watch' and restores 'Nobody trips.', the small turn that keeps the still from being solemn.

Critic suggestion: Four banners fly from the same pole. It is a little crowded, and nobody minds.
Why: Restores 'and nobody minds', which says the whole ending in five words.

Critic suggestion: At the edge of the crowd, a hooded traveler smiles, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
Why: Drops 'you see'; the traveler is the player, so narrating that 'you see' him reads oddly.

Critic suggestion: Get up, Dad. You're going to {town}. Agnes has a form for you, Maren has a great deal to say, and you are going to listen to all of it.
Why: Story files use the token, not the literal town name (canon rule; renders the same).

Critic suggestion: No. It was yours too. Get up. You're going to {town}, and you're going to listen to every word Maren says.
Why: Story files use the token, not the literal town name (canon rule; renders the same).
